proof:
# Nonlocal canonical domination when all proper traces are vertex caps

This is a proved subclass of the arbitrary-radius angular-normal question. It does not assert that every actual critical cap belongs to the subclass. Full and empty traces are allowed, integer dimension is arbitrary, and the radius array need not be close to an even array. A cap outside the subclass may have proper traces containing several simplex vertices; no conclusion is supplied for that mixed regime.

## 1. Precise theorem

Let d>=2, let T be a centered d-simplex of volume V with vertices v_0,...,v_d, and let a finite family of positive homothetic fibers r_z T sit at bases z in P subset Z^n. Suppose z_0 is in P. If desired these may be the complete fibers of an actual convex body; the comparison below preserves that same body and needs no additional hypothesis on the radius array.

Fix a nonvertical halfspace through the ACTUAL point (z_0,0):

    H={u.x+alpha.(z-z_0)>=0},  u!=0.

Assume every proper positive-volume trace H intersect (r_z T) is a one-vertex simplex cap at the same unique maximizing vertex v_0 of u. More precisely, put

    H_0=u.v_0>u.v_j=h_j (j=1,...,d),
    k_z=alpha.(z-z_0),  t_z=H_0 r_z+k_z,
    Delta_j=H_0-h_j.

Every fiber is required to have either zero captured volume, full captured volume, or

    0<t_z<=r_z min_j Delta_j.                       (1)

The equality in (1) allows the cutting plane to contain another original vertex; it still has the same exact simplex-cap volume. Since the simplex is centered, H_0>0 and sum_j Delta_j=(d+1)H_0.

Let u_can be the unique linear functional taking value d at v_0 and -1 at the other vertices. Define

    beta=(d/H_0)alpha,
    H_can={u_can.x+beta.(z-z_0)>=0}.                 (2)

Then H_can passes through the SAME mixed-integer point and

    mu(S intersect H_can)<=mu(S intersect H).       (3)

If u is not a positive multiple of u_can, the inequality is strict. Thus an actual depth-attaining cap through a fiber centroid cannot have a noncanonical continuous normal while every one of its proper traces is a same-vertex cap. This is an actual all-fiber replacement, not an independently chosen direction or tilt in each fiber.

## 2. Proof, including full and empty traces

For a trace satisfying (1), its d edge intercept fractions from r_z v_0 are t_z/(r_z Delta_j). Hence its exact captured volume is

    V t_z^d/product_j Delta_j.                      (4)

The new canonical cap's apex height is

    d r_z+beta.(z-z_0)=(d/H_0)t_z.

For every real value of this height, its ACTUAL captured volume is

    V min{r_z^d, [((d/H_0)t_z)_+/(d+1)]^d}.        (5)

This formula includes empty and full saturation. In particular, it is at most V Gamma_d(t_z/H_0)^d when t_z>0. AM-GM and sum Delta_j=(d+1)H_0 give

    product_j Delta_j<=((d+1)H_0/d)^d,

so (5) is at most (4). An originally empty trace has t_z<=0, because v_0 is the unique maximum; the new trace is empty as well (or only supporting, still zero volume). An originally full trace can only lose mass, since the new trace is always a subset of the same full fiber. Thus every original fiber individually satisfies the desired comparison, and their actual sum proves (3).

At the source z_0, the original cap is proper: 0 is in the interior of r_(z_0)T and u!=0. Therefore it is one of the caps in (1). Here t_(z_0)=H_0 r_(z_0). The new cap is the ordinary canonical centroid cap, with volume Gamma_d V r_(z_0)^d. If u is not canonical, the d positive numbers Delta_j are not all equal. AM-GM is strict, so the source-fiber comparison is strict. This proves the strict global claim.

The same proof permits an affine centroid graph c_z=A z+b. The actual ambient shear x -> x-Az-b preserves the mixed-integer lattice and every fiber measure. It does not permit nonaffine recentering of a common-vertex radius family.

## 3. Complete canonical and opposite-canonical scalar functionals

For centered standard simplex coordinates v_0=(-1,...,-1), v_i=v_0+(d+1)e_i, and any anchor z_0, every canonical vertex direction has the SAME complete cap functional

    Q_+(beta)=V sum_(z in P)
       min{r_z^d, [(d r_z+beta.(z-z_0))_+/(d+1)]^d}. (6)

This retains every full, empty, proper, and supporting trace. The opposite-canonical direction has functional

    Q_-(beta)=M-Q_+(-beta),
    M=V sum_z r_z^d.                                (7)

Equation (7) uses only that nonvertical hyperplane boundaries have zero d-volume in every positive fiber; it does not discard the mass of a purely integer boundary. Such vertical caps can always be replaced by finite tilts of a fixed canonical direction at no larger mass, because their whole boundary fibers become subsets and their strict full/empty fibers keep their status.

For arbitrary integer n, (6) is a continuous piecewise degree-d polynomial on the finite arrangement of affine hyperplanes

    beta.(z-z_0)=-d r_z,
    beta.(z-z_0)=r_z.

The finite-base bounded-tilt representative lemma gives an attained minimum on a fixed compact representative set. The minimum over just the canonical and opposite-canonical family is therefore the exact finite problem

    min{min_beta Q_+(beta), M-max_beta Q_+(beta)}.    (8)

This is not asserted to equal the unrestricted mixed depth for every radius array. The theorem proves that any excluded noncanonical minimizer must have at least one genuinely multi-vertex proper trace. The common-vertex unequal-normal stationary example in `candidate 6683db9073239231` does not contradict this theorem: its nonaffine radius changes its centroid graph, so it cannot be centered by an allowed affine shear.

## 4. Boundary and scope checks

All original points, bodies, bases, and fibers remain fixed in the replacement. Only one actual ambient halfspace is changed. The new integer normal is one common scalar multiple of the old normal. There is no transformation of integer coordinates or independent per-fiber optimization. Every point source is a single original centroid in S. Equalities at a simplex support plane retain their correct zero or full volume. For d=1 the angular distinction disappears; the statement is restricted to d>=2 because its useful strict AM-GM conclusion has no one-number analogue.
